Summary: Connect success notification for a non-secure (HTTP) IEEE2030.5 connection.
Preconditions: 1. IEEE2030.5 client configured in non-secure mode; server reachable.
Actions: 1. Start the connection to a reachable server.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays a CONNECT success notification.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a connect success notification for a secure (HTTPS/TLS) IEEE2030.5 connection with a valid, trusted server certificate and matching hostname.
Preconditions: Server certificate signed by a trusted CA; certificate CN/SAN matches the configured hostname; Trust Server Cert option OFF.
Actions: 1. Start the connection to the server.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays a CONNECT success notification (CONNECT: Notification).

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a connect success notification when Trust Server Cert option is enabled, even if the server certificate would otherwise fail validation.
Preconditions: Trust Server Cert option enabled; server presents any certificate (including untrusted/invalid).
Actions: 1. Start secure connection to server.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays a CONNECT success notification (CONNECT: Notification).

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a connect failure notification with reason when the target server refuses the connection (no service listening).
Preconditions: Valid host/IP with no service listening on the configured port.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a human-readable reason (e.g. connection refused) and the underlying error code.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a connect failure notification with reason when the target host/IP is unreachable.
Preconditions: Unreachable/blackholed IP address configured.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a timeout/unreachable reason and the underlying error code.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a connect failure notification with reason when the configured hostname cannot be resolved via DNS.
Preconditions: Non-existent hostname configured.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a DNS/name resolution reason and the underlying error code.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a connect failure notification with reason when connecting to a valid host on a closed port.
Preconditions: Valid host with the configured port closed/not listening.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a connection-refused reason and the underlying error code.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a specific certificate failure reason (invalid/untrusted CA) when the server presents a certificate signed by an untrusted CA.
Preconditions: Server certificate signed by an untrusted/self-signed CA not in the trust store; Trust Server Cert OFF.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a reason indicating the certificate chain terminates in an untrusted root (invalid CA).

Summary: Verify user prompt and successful connection when hostname/CN mismatch occurs for IEEE2030.5 protocol with Trust Server Cert OFF, and user accepts the mismatch.
Preconditions: Server certificate CN/SAN does not match configured hostname; protocol = IEEE2030.5; Trust Server Cert OFF.
Actions: 3. When prompted, accept the hostname mismatch.
Expected Results: A hostname mismatch popup is shown; upon accepting, the connection succeeds and line monitor displays CONNECT success notification.

Summary: Verify connection failure and reason when hostname/CN mismatch occurs for IEEE2030.5 protocol and the user rejects the mismatch prompt.
Preconditions: Server certificate CN/SAN does not match configured hostname; protocol = IEEE2030.5; Trust Server Cert OFF.
Actions: 3. When prompted, reject the hostname mismatch.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a cancellation/CN mismatch reason; connection does not proceed.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a CN-invalid failure reason (no popup) when hostname/CN mismatch occurs for a non-IEEE2030.5 protocol, or when Trust Server Cert is ON.
Preconditions: Server certificate CN/SAN mismatch configured; either protocol is not IEEE2030.5, or Trust Server Cert is ON.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: No popup is shown; line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a reason indicating the certificate common name (hostname) is incorrect.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a specific certificate failure reason when the server certificate is expired or not yet valid.
Preconditions: Server certificate with notAfter in the past (or notBefore in the future).
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a reason indicating the certificate date is invalid (expired/not yet valid).

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a specific certificate failure reason when the server certificate has been revoked.
Preconditions: Server certificate revoked; revocation checking (CRL/OCSP) enabled and reachable.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a reason indicating the certificate was revoked.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a specific failure reason when the certificate revocation check itself cannot be performed (e.g. CRL/OCSP endpoint unreachable).
Preconditions: Revocation checking enabled; CRL/OCSP endpoint unreachable/blocked.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a reason indicating the revocation check could not be performed.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows a specific failure reason when the server presents a broken/incomplete certificate chain (intermediate certificate issue) or otherwise invalid certificate.
Preconditions: Server certificate chain missing/incorrect intermediate certificate, or otherwise malformed/unsupported certificate.
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with a reason indicating the certificate is invalid.

Summary: Verify line monitor shows the first applicable failure reason (per defined priority order) when the server certificate is invalid in more than one way simultaneously.
Preconditions: Server certificate constructed to be invalid in multiple ways (e.g. CN mismatch and invalid CA).
Actions: 1. Attempt to connect.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays CONNECT Failed with the reason corresponding to the first matching check in priority order: revocation check failed, invalid CA, CN invalid, date invalid, revoked, invalid cert.

Summary: Verify no premature success/failure message is shown while an asynchronous connect attempt is still pending.
Preconditions: Slow-responding server causing the WinHTTP connect to return a pending (WSAEWOULDBLOCK) state.
Actions: 2. Attempt to connect and observe the line monitor while the connection is pending.
Expected Results: No CONNECT success or failure message is inserted until the connection outcome (success/failure) is actually known.

Summary: Regression: verify the existing disconnect notification in the line monitor is unaffected by the new connect success/failure messages.
Preconditions: An established IEEE2030.5 connection.
Actions: 2. Disconnect the connection.
Expected Results: Line monitor displays the existing disconnect notification as before, unaffected by the new connect messages.

Summary: Verify that after a failed connection attempt, a subsequent retry produces a fresh, independent success/failure message with no stale state carried over.
Preconditions: A prior failed connection attempt.
Actions: 2. Retry the connection (fix the condition causing failure, e.g. start the server).
Expected Results: Line monitor shows a fresh CONNECT success (or failure) message for the retry, independent of the previous failure message.

Summary: Verify that the Restart() connect code path produces the same CONNECT success/failure line monitor messages as the Start() code path.
Preconditions: An IEEE2030.5 monitor that has been started and is being restarted (e.g. configuration change).
Actions: 2. Observe the line monitor for each case.
Expected Results: The Restart() path shows the same CONNECT success/failure notifications (with reason, where applicable) as the Start() path.

Summary: To verify a schema-valid Subscription POST is constructed per device with all mandatory fields
Preconditions: A simulated device has discovered a subscribable FSAL/DER Program List/DER Control List resource (`subscribable="1"`)
Actions:
1. Start the test set with an IEEE 2030.5 device configured against a server exposing a subscribable resource.
2. Allow discovery/polling to run until the resource is read.
3. Capture the outgoing Subscription POST body.
Expected Results: The POST body contains `subscribedResource`, `notificationURI`, `encoding`, `level`, and `limit`, and validates against the sep-2018 Subscription schema

Summary: To verify a resource advertising `subscribable="1"` triggers a Subscription POST
Preconditions: Server resource list entry has `subscribable` attribute set to `1`
Actions:
1. Run discovery against the resource.
2. Observe whether a Subscription POST is issued.
Expected Results: Subscription POST is sent

Summary: To verify poll-only fallback when a resource does not advertise subscribable support
Preconditions: Server resource list entry has `subscribable` absent, empty, `"*"`, or `"0"`
Actions:
1. Run discovery against the resource.
2. Observe whether a Subscription POST is issued.
3. Confirm the resource continues to be GET-polled at its normal rate.
Expected Results: No Subscription POST is sent for that resource; the device continues normal GET-based polling of it indefinitely

Summary: To verify rejection of a subscription request at creation time is handled as a distinct failure path, with normal polling continuing
Preconditions: Server configured to reject new Subscription POSTs (e.g. resource not found, 404, or subscription limit already exceeded, e.g. 400/403)
Actions:
1. Trigger a fresh Subscription POST for a previously-unsubscribed resource.
2. Server responds with a non-201 status.
3. Observe subsequent polling and retry behavior.
Expected Results: The resource is NOT added to `m_SubscribedResourceHrefs`; normal GET polling continues uninterrupted; the dedup key is recorded in a reject-backoff map so the identical POST is not retried on every subsequent discovery/poll

Summary: To verify a rejected subscription is retried after the defined backoff period elapses
Preconditions: A resource's Subscription POST was previously rejected (per TID-2190.6)
Actions:
1. Wait for the reject-backoff interval (5 minutes) to elapse.
2. Trigger another discovery/poll cycle for the same resource.
3. Observe whether a new Subscription POST is sent.
Expected Results: `IsSubscriptionRejectBackoffActive()` returns FALSE once 5 minutes have elapsed; a fresh Subscription POST is dispatched for the same resource

Summary: To verify an active subscription is automatically renewed before it lapses
Preconditions: A resource has an active (201-accepted) subscription recorded in `m_SubscribedResourceHrefs`
Actions:
1. Allow the subscription to remain active until the renewal interval elapses.
2. Observe whether a new Subscription POST (re-POST) is sent for the same resource without user action.
Expected Results: `IsSubscriptionRenewalDue()` returns TRUE once the renewal interval has elapsed since last (re)dispatch; `PostSubscription()` falls through and re-POSTs exactly like a fresh subscribe; the dedup timestamp is restamped on success

Summary: To verify an active, non-expiring subscription is not redundantly re-posted
Preconditions: A resource has an active subscription that has not yet reached the renewal interval
Actions:
1. Poll/discover the same resource repeatedly before the renewal interval elapses.
2. Observe whether additional Subscription POSTs are sent.
Expected Results: `PostSubscription()` returns as a no-op (`alreadySubscribed && !renewalDue`); no duplicate Subscription POST is sent

Summary: To verify a single "Post Subscription" exchange is reused for every subscribe/renew/unsubscribe call across all devices/resources
Preconditions: Multiple devices each with one or more subscribable resources (FSAL, DER Program List, DER Control List)
Actions:
1. Allow subscriptions to be created and renewed for multiple devices/resources over an extended run.
2. Inspect the exchange list in the UI/configuration.
Expected Results: Only one "Post Subscription" exchange row exists in the exchange list regardless of how many subscribe/renew/unsubscribe events have occurred; no new exchange rows accumulate per event

Summary: To verify concurrent subscription requests sharing the single exchange do not corrupt each other or get applied to the wrong resource
Preconditions: Two or more devices/resources become eligible for subscription POSTs at approximately the same time
Actions:
1. Trigger near-simultaneous subscription-eligible conditions for two different clients/resources.
2. Capture each outgoing Subscription POST body and its corresponding response handling.
Expected Results: Each POST body's `subscribedResource` href corresponds to the correct originating resource; no cross-contamination of hrefs/clients occurs; the shared exchange's dedup/in-flight tracking (`m_SubscriptionInFlightClients`, `m_PendingSubscriptionQueueByClient`) correctly serializes/queues requests per client without applying one client's response to another

Summary: To verify a stalled/unresponsive subscription POST does not permanently block subsequent subscription requests
Preconditions: A client's in-flight Subscription POST never receives a response (simulate dropped connection/server hang)
Actions:
1. Trigger a Subscription POST and prevent/delay the server's response indefinitely.
2. Wait beyond the stall timeout (60 seconds).
3. Trigger a new subscription-eligible condition for the same client.
Expected Results: `IsSubscriptionStalled()` returns TRUE after 60 seconds of no response; the stale in-flight state is cleared; the new request is dispatched immediately rather than queuing behind the dead request indefinitely

Summary: To verify a second subscription-eligible resource queues properly behind an in-flight (but not stalled) request for the same client
Preconditions: Client already has one in-flight Subscription POST awaiting response (within stall timeout)
Actions:
1. Trigger a second subscription-eligible resource for the same client while the first POST is still in-flight.
2. Observe queuing behavior.
3. Allow the first response to arrive.
Expected Results: The second request is added to `m_PendingSubscriptionQueueByClient` rather than dispatched immediately; once the first in-flight POST resolves, the queued request is dispatched

Summary: To verify unchecking "DER FSA List" prevents Function Set Assignments List subscriptions while leaving other resource types unaffected
Preconditions: `SubscribeFSAL` option unchecked; `SubscribeDERProgramList`/`SubscribeDERControlList` checked; device has all three resource types available and subscribable
Actions:
1. Uncheck "DER FSA List" in the protocol options UI (Subscribable Resources group box).
2. Run the device.
3. Observe whether a Subscription POST is sent for the FSAL resource vs. the DER Program List/DER Control List resources.
Expected Results: No Subscription POST is sent for the FSAL resource (falls back to poll-only); Subscription POSTs are still sent normally for DER Program List and DER Control List resources

Summary: To verify unchecking "DER Program List" prevents only DER Program List subscriptions
Preconditions: `SubscribeDERProgramList` unchecked; other two checked
Actions:
1. Uncheck "DER Program List".
2. Run the device.
3. Observe subscription POSTs per resource type.
Expected Results: No Subscription POST sent for DER Program List resource; FSAL and DER Control List subscriptions proceed normally

Summary: To verify unchecking "DER Control List" prevents only DER Control List subscriptions
Preconditions: `SubscribeDERControlList` unchecked; other two checked
Actions:
1. Uncheck "DER Control List".
2. Run the device.
3. Observe subscription POSTs per resource type.
Expected Results: No Subscription POST sent for DER Control List resource; FSAL and DER Program List subscriptions proceed normally

Summary: To verify all three subscribable-resource checkboxes default to checked (subscribe to everything) on a new/upgraded project
Preconditions: New project created, or an older project file lacking the new TSOptions attributes is loaded
Actions:
1. Create a new protocol configuration (or load a pre-existing project predating this feature).
2. Open the IEEE 2030.5 protocol options page.
3. Inspect the three checkbox states.
Expected Results: "DER FSA List", "DER Program List", and "DER Control List" checkboxes are all checked by default, preserving prior (subscribe-to-everything) behavior

Summary: To verify the three subscribable-resource options are correctly exported/imported via CSV
Preconditions: A project with a non-default combination of the three checkboxes (e.g. only FSAL checked)
Actions:
1. Export the project configuration to CSV.
2. Inspect the CSV for `IEEE20305.SubscribeFSAL`/`SubscribeDERProgramList`/`SubscribeDERControlList` entries.
3. Import the CSV into a fresh project.
4. Re-open the protocol options page.
Expected Results: CSV contains correct boolean values for all three properties; after import, the checkbox states match the originally exported configuration exactly

Summary: To verify the subscribable-resource toggle setting applies globally to all clients/devices, not per-client
Preconditions: Multiple simulated End Devices configured under the same IEEE 2030.5 protocol instance, each with subscribable FSAL resources
Actions:
1. Uncheck "DER FSA List" once at the protocol level.
2. Run multiple devices under that protocol instance.
3. Observe FSAL subscription behavior across all devices.
Expected Results: No device under that protocol instance posts an FSAL subscription; the setting is not configurable independently per device/client

Summary: To verify a per-device subscription record file is created on disk when a Subscription POST is accepted
Preconditions: A simulated device has an eligible subscribable resource and no prior `.sub` record file exists for it under the SubscriptionRepo folder
Actions:
1. Start the test set with an IEEE 2030.5 device configured against a server that accepts Subscription POSTs (201 Created).
2. Allow discovery/polling to trigger a Subscription POST for a resource.
3. Wait for the server's 201 Created response.
4. Inspect `C:\ProgramData\Applied Systems Engineering\ASE 2000 V2 Communications Test Set\SubscriptionRepo\<EntryEndDeviceID>.sub`.
Expected Results: A `.sub` file for that device's `EntryEndDeviceID` is created immediately upon the 201 response, containing a line with the resource's `Href`, the server-assigned `SubscriptionLink` (Location header), and a `TimestampTick`

Summary: To verify no subscription record is written when a Subscription POST is rejected
Preconditions: Server configured to reject a Subscription POST (e.g. 400/403/404)
Actions:
1. Trigger a fresh Subscription POST for a previously-unsubscribed resource.
2. Server responds with a non-201 status.
3. Inspect the device's `.sub` file (or confirm none exists).
Expected Results: No record for that resource's `Href` is added to the device's `.sub` file; if the file did not previously exist, it is still not created by this rejected attempt

Summary: To verify re-subscribing to an already-recorded resource updates its existing entry instead of creating a duplicate
Preconditions: A resource already has an accepted subscription recorded in the device's `.sub` file (per TID-2461.1)
Actions:
1. Allow the existing subscription to be renewed (or manually force a re-POST for the same `Href`) so the server returns a new 201 Created with a different `SubscriptionLink`.
2. Inspect the device's `.sub` file after the new acceptance.
Expected Results: The `.sub` file still contains exactly one line for that `Href`; `SubscriptionLink` and `TimestampTick` are updated to the new values; no second/duplicate line for the same `Href` is appended

Summary: To verify each device's subscription records are persisted to its own isolated file, not a shared global file
Preconditions: Two or more simulated devices (distinct EntryEndDeviceID values), each with at least one accepted subscription
Actions:
1. Allow each device to successfully subscribe to at least one resource.
2. Inspect the SubscriptionRepo folder contents.
Expected Results: A separate `<EntryEndDeviceID>.sub` file exists per device; each file contains only the records belonging to that device's own `EntryEndDeviceID`; no cross-device record contamination occurs

Summary: To verify the on-disk record is updated immediately (write-through) on every accepted subscribe/renew, not batched or delayed
Preconditions: A resource is about to receive an accepted (201) Subscription POST response
Actions:
1. Trigger a Subscription POST for a resource and capture the exact moment the 201 Created response is processed.
2. Immediately (without waiting for any additional polling cycle) inspect the `.sub` file's last-modified timestamp and content.
Expected Results: The `.sub` file is updated (new/changed `mtime`, content reflecting the just-accepted record) synchronously as part of handling that single response, with no observable delay or batching window

Summary: To verify the SubscriptionRepo folder is created automatically if it does not already exist
Preconditions: The `SubscriptionRepo` folder under ProgramData does not exist prior to the first subscription accept
Actions:
1. Ensure the SubscriptionRepo folder is absent (delete it if present from a prior run).
2. Trigger a subscription accept for any device/resource.
3. Inspect ProgramData for the folder's existence.
Expected Results: The `SubscriptionRepo` folder is created automatically on first use; the record file is successfully written inside it without requiring any manual setup

Summary: To verify concurrent write-through persistence for multiple devices subscribing at nearly the same time does not corrupt or cross-write records
Preconditions: Two or more devices become eligible for accepted subscriptions at approximately the same time
Actions:
1. Trigger near-simultaneous subscription acceptances for two different devices (different EntryEndDeviceIDs).
2. Inspect both devices' `.sub` files afterward.
Expected Results: Each device's `.sub` file contains only its own correct record(s); the per-device file path (keyed by `EntryEndDeviceID`) and the `m_ExchPtrLock`-guarded in-memory map prevent one device's concurrent write from corrupting or overwriting another device's file

Summary: To verify the in-memory subscription record mirror stays consistent with the on-disk file after multiple upserts for the same device
Preconditions: A device has multiple distinct subscribable resources, each independently accepted over time
Actions:
1. Allow several different resources on the same device to each receive an accepted (201) Subscription POST, one after another.
2. After each acceptance, inspect the device's `.sub` file content.
Expected Results: Each new resource's record is appended as a new line (since it is a distinct `Href`); previously recorded resources' lines remain unchanged; the file always reflects the full, current in-memory record set for that device after each write-through

Summary: To verify a failed persistence write (e.g. folder inaccessible) degrades gracefully without crashing the application or blocking subscription acceptance in memory
Preconditions: The SubscriptionRepo folder (or its parent) is made read-only/inaccessible prior to a subscription accept
Actions:
1. Make the SubscriptionRepo folder read-only or otherwise deny write access.
2. Trigger a subscription accept (201 Created) for a resource on that device.
3. Observe application stability and in-memory subscription state.
Expected Results: `SaveSubscriptionRecords()` returns `FALSE` without throwing or crashing the application; the in-memory subscription state (`m_SubscribedResourceHrefs`, dedup/renewal tracking) is still correctly updated so the resource continues to behave as subscribed for the remainder of the session, even though the on-disk file could not be updated

Summary: To verify the "Delete Subscription" exchange can still be sent manually and produces a well-formed DELETE request, even though its response is not automatically wired to remove a persisted record
Preconditions: A device has an active subscription with a known `SubscriptionLink`; the "Delete Subscription" exchange is available in the exchange list
Actions:
1. Manually populate the "Delete Subscription" exchange's `Link` field with the subscription's URL.
2. Manually send the exchange.
3. Capture the outgoing request and the server's response.
Expected Results: A correctly formed DELETE request (no body, target URL from the `Link` field) is transmitted and the server's response is received normally; the device's `.sub` file is NOT automatically updated to remove the corresponding record (deletion/reconciliation wiring is explicitly out of scope for this story) - record cleanup, if desired, must be handled manually or by a future story

Summary: Verify that accepted subscription records are retained after restarting ASE2000.
Preconditions: A device has multiple accepted subscriptions saved in its .sub file.
Actions: 1. Create subscriptions for multiple resources. 2. Verify that their records are saved to disk. 3. Close ASE2000 normally and restart it. 4. Reconnect the device and inspect the subscription state.
Expected Results: Persisted records are loaded correctly after restart. Existing valid subscriptions are recognized without unnecessary duplicate subscriptions.

Summary: The listener opens its port only when the first Post Subscription of a Start or Send Continuous session is built. Other exchanges, with Send Once or Send Continuous, never open it.
Preconditions:
At least one of Subscribe FSAL / Subscribe DERProgramList / Subscribe DERControlList selected in Tools->Properties (all three are selected by default).
Listener certificate,ASE2K2030DC000003-SERCA-MICA-DC.p12 present at "C:\ProgramData\Applied Systems Engineering\ASE 2000 V2 Communications Test Set\P12repo" and its 2030.5 root/MICA installed in the Windows certificate stores.
Messages: when the listener opens, the Messages tab shows IEEE 2030.5 notification listener: listening on https port [N], notification path /ntfy/[T] (once per session). A Post Subscription that cannot get a listener is not sent and shows Subscription not sent: IEEE 2030.5 notification listener not started, [reason]. on every attempt.
Actions:
1. Send Once on Read DeviceCapability and Read EndDevice, then Send Continuous on Read DeviceCapability for about 10 seconds and Stop. After each, List the listening ports of the ASE2000 process: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen -OwningProcess (Get-Process -Name 'ASE 2000 Communication Test Set').Id
2. Start the session. While discovery is still before any Post Subscription, list the ports again.
3. Let discovery reach the first Post Subscription; read the Messages tab and list the ports.
Expected Results:
1. Steps 1-2: no listener port, no IEEE 2030.5 notification listener line and no Subscription not sent line.
2. Step 3: IEEE 2030.5 notification listener: listening on https port [N], notification path /ntfy/[16 hex characters] appears exactly once and port [N] is listening.
3. [N] is between 2500 and 65534.
4. The client channels connect and poll as without the listener.

Summary: All aggregators of a session share one listener: one port and one token, however many devices and Post Subscription exchanges there are.
Preconditions:
Configuration with at least two aggregators (each with end devices), all over HTTPS, subscriptions selected in Tools->Properties.
Listener certificate,ASE2K2030DC000003-SERCA-MICA-DC.p12 present at "C:\ProgramData\Applied Systems Engineering\ASE 2000 V2 Communications Test Set\P12repo" and its 2030.5 root/MICA installed in the Windows certificate stores.
A 2030.5 server (or test server) that returns the EndDevice with a SubscriptionListLink and answers Subscription POSTs.
Messages: when the listener opens, the Messages tab shows IEEE 2030.5 notification listener: listening on https port [N], notification path /ntfy/[T] (once per session). A Post Subscription that cannot get a listener is not sent and shows Subscription not sent: IEEE 2030.5 notification listener not started, [reason]. on every attempt.
Actions:
1. Start the session and let discovery send a Post Subscription for every client (Post Subscription and Post Subscription_[clientID]).
2. Count the listening on lines and List the listening ports of the ASE2000 process: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen -OwningProcess (Get-Process -Name 'ASE 2000 Communication Test Set').Id
3. Open the notificationURI of every transmitted Post Subscription request.
Expected Results:
1. One listening on line and one listener port for the whole session.
2. Every request carries the same port [N] and token [T]; only the host can differ (the local address that reaches each server).

Summary: Stop closes the listener and releases its port. The next session opens a new listener on a new random port with a new token and overwrites the notificationURI, so a Notification for the earlier session is never taken as current: it is refused, or answered with 400 so the server removes that subscription (IEEE 2030.5 8.7 rule o).
Preconditions:
Session running with the listener started (TC NtfyListener-OpensOnFirstPostSubscription); port [N] and token [T] noted from the listening on line. Call them [N1] and [T1].
Test client script Testplan\ASE-2405_NotificationListenerTestClient.ps1 (plays the 2030.5 server). Device certificate [AGG2] = C:\ProgramData\Applied Systems Engineering\ASE 2000 V2 Communications Test Set\P12repo\ASE2K2030AGGR000002-SERCA-MICA-DC.p12.
Actions:
1. Stop the session; List the listening ports of the ASE2000 process: Get-NetTCPConnection -State Listen -OwningProcess (Get-Process -Name 'ASE 2000 Communication Test Set').Id
2. POST to port [N1] path /ntfy/[T1].
3. Start again, let discovery send Post Subscription and note [N2] / [T2]; open the transmitted request.
4. POST to port [N2] with path /ntfy/[T1], then with /ntfy/[T2].
Expected Results:
1. Step 1: port [N1] is released; Stop completes without delay.
2. Step 2: FAILED (connection refused).
3. Step 3: [T2] differs from [T1], [N2] is in 2500-65534 and normally differs from [N1]; the request carries [N2]/[T2], never the old URI.
4. Step 4: /ntfy/[T1] gets HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request; /ntfy/[T2] gets HTTP/1.1 201 Created.

Summary: With no resource type selected for subscription, a Start session sends no Subscription and opens no listener, so poll-only behaviour is unchanged (REQID-ASE-2190-4.5).
Preconditions:
IEEE 2030.5 HTTPS client configuration.
Messages: when the listener opens, the Messages tab shows IEEE 2030.5 notification listener: listening on https port [N], notification path /ntfy/[T] (once per session). A Post Subscription that cannot get a listener is not sent and shows Subscription not sent: IEEE 2030.5 notification listener not started, [reason]. on every attempt.
Actions:
1. In Tools->Properties clear Subscribe FSAL, Subscribe DERProgramList and Subscribe DERControlList.
2. Start the session and let discovery run through FSA, DERProgramList and DERControlList.
3. Check the message view, the Messages tab and the listening ports.
Expected Results:
1. No Post Subscription is sent; no listener line and no Subscription not sent line appear.
2. No listener port is opened.
3. Polling works exactly as before the feature.

Summary: Several ASE2000 instances on one machine each run their own listener on their own port, without conflicts.
Preconditions:
Two ASE2000 instances (A and B), each with an IEEE 2030.5 HTTPS client configuration and subscriptions selected.
Listener certificate,ASE2K2030DC000003-SERCA-MICA-DC.p12 present at "C:\ProgramData\Applied Systems Engineering\ASE 2000 V2 Communications Test Set\P12repo" and its 2030.5 root/MICA installed in the Windows certificate stores.
Test client script Testplan\ASE-2405_NotificationListenerTestClient.ps1 (plays the 2030.5 server). Device certificate [AGG2] = C:\ProgramData\Applied Systems Engineering\ASE 2000 V2 Communications Test Set\P12repo\ASE2K2030AGGR000002-SERCA-MICA-DC.p12.
Actions:
1. Start the session in A, then in B; let both reach Post Subscription and note port and token of each.
2. POST to each instance's own port and token, then to A's port with B's token.
Expected Results:
1. Both listeners start on different ports.
2. Each instance answers 201 Created for its own port and token; the mixed request gets 400.
3. Neither instance's client channels are affected by the other.

Summary: The Subscription POSTed by a Start session carries the running listener as notificationURI (https://[local address]:[port]/ntfy/[token]) with the local address that reaches that server, and the value sent is written into the exchange so Object Properties shows it.
Preconditions:
At least one of Subscribe FSAL / Subscribe DERProgramList / Subscribe DERControlList selected in Tools->Properties (all three are selected by default).
Listener certificate,ASE2K2030DC000003-SERCA-MICA-DC.p12 present at "C:\ProgramData\Applied Systems Engineering\ASE 2000 V2 Communications Test Set\P12repo" and its 2030.5 root/MICA installed in the Windows certificate stores.
A 2030.5 server (or test server) that returns the EndDevice with a SubscriptionListLink and answers Subscription POSTs.
Messages: when the listener opens, the Messages tab shows IEEE 2030.5 notification listener: listening on https port [N], notification path /ntfy/[T] (once per session). A Post Subscription that cannot get a listener is not sent and shows Subscription not sent: IEEE 2030.5 notification listener not started, [reason]. on every attempt.
Actions:
1. Start the session and note port [N] and token [T].
2. Let discovery run (DeviceCapability, EndDeviceList, EndDevice, FSA, DER lists).

Summary: When a DERControl is first discovered/spawned, the client must send a "received" DERControlResponse immediately, before waiting for the event's StartTime to arrive.
Preconditions: Server has an active DERControlList with a control whose StartTime is in the future. Time resource has already been read successfully from this server.
Actions:
1. Configure/run a DERProgram exchange that discovers a DERControl scheduled to start later.
2. Allow the tool to dynamically spawn the Execute DER Control exchange.
3. Observe the first POST DERControlResponse sent by the tool.
4. Wait until the control's StartTime arrives and observe the next POST.
Expected Results: The first DERControlResponse POST reports currentStatus = "Event received" immediately on discovery, prior to StartTime. A second, separate DERControlResponse reporting "Event started" is sent only once StartTime is reached.

Summary: Once a DERControl's window opens (now >= StartTime), the client must report "Event started" exactly once, and only if the server requested a specific response.
Preconditions: A DERControl has already been acknowledged as "received" and its StartTime has just elapsed. responseRequired requests specific responses.
Actions:
1. Let the previously-received control's StartTime elapse.
2. Observe the DERControlResponse POST generated on the next tick.
3. Continue polling and observe subsequent ticks while the control remains active.
Expected Results: Exactly one DERControlResponse with currentStatus = "Event started" (status 2) is sent when the window opens. No further "started" responses are sent on subsequent polls while the control remains active without a new transition.

Summary: All acknowledgement transitions (received, started, completed/cancelled/superseded) for a given DERControl must be sent using the same dynamically-created Execute DER Control exchange rather than spawning a new exchange per transition.
Preconditions: A DERControl is discovered and dynamically spawns an Execute DER Control child exchange.
Actions:
1. Trigger the received, started, and completed transitions for the same DERControl in sequence (allow the full window to elapse).
2. Inspect the Exchange list / Messages tab for the exchange name associated with each POST.
Expected Results: All three DERControlResponse POSTs (received, started, completed) are sent from the same single "Execute DER Control" exchange instance for that control; no additional duplicate exchanges are created for later transitions.

Summary: The Read DER Control List exchange must read its own pollRate value from its response body rather than falling back to the pollRate configured on its parent Read DER Program List exchange.
Preconditions: Server responds to Read DER Control List with a pollRate value that differs from the parent Read DER Program List's pollRate.
Actions:
1. Configure the server/simulated response so DERControlList's pollRate differs from DERProgramList's pollRate.
2. Run the Read DER Program List exchange followed by Read DER Control List.
3. Inspect the poll interval used for subsequent Read DER Control List requests.
Expected Results: Read DER Control List polls at the interval specified by its own response's pollRate attribute, not the pollRate inherited from the parent Read DER Program List exchange.

Summary: Per IEEE 2030.5 9.2.3, the client must not act on (execute/acknowledge) a DERControl until a Time resource has been successfully retrieved from the same server.
Preconditions: A DERControlList response with a schedulable control is available, but the Read Time exchange for this server has not yet been run/completed.
Actions:
1. Discover a DERControl without first running the Read Time exchange for that server.
2. Observe whether any DERControlResponse POST is attempted.
3. Then run the Read Time exchange for the server and observe behavior afterward.
Expected Results: No DERControlResponse is sent while no valid Time resource exists for the server; an informational message is logged/suppressed rather than a transmit error. Once Time is retrieved, scheduling resumes and the appropriate response (received/started) is sent on the next tick.

Summary: When a DERControl's effective expiry time is reached without cancellation/supersession, the client must transition it to Complete and, if requested, send a single "completed" DERControlResponse.
Preconditions: A DERControl is active and its EffectiveExpiry/ExpiryTime is approaching.
Actions:
1. Allow an active DERControl to run until its EffectiveExpiry time is reached.
2. Observe the DERControlResponse POST generated on/after that tick.
3. Continue polling afterward and observe subsequent ticks.
Expected Results: Exactly one DERControlResponse with currentStatus = "Event completed" is sent once EffectiveExpiry is reached (if a specific response was requested); no further responses are sent for that control on later polls.

Summary: When a DERControl's schedule window ends normally (EffectiveExpiry reached), the control must transition to Complete, report once if requested, and be retired from the active schedule.
Preconditions: An active DERControl with a resolved schedule (StartTime != 0) is running, with a valid Time source established for the server.
Actions:
1. Let the active DERControl run until now >= EffectiveExpiry.
2. Observe the DERControlResponse POST (if any) on that tick.
3. Inspect the exchange's name/state and timer status afterward.
4. Continue polling and observe subsequent ticks.
Expected Results: DERCtrlState transitions to COMPLETE; a single "completed" DERControlResponse is sent if responseRequired's specific bit is set. RetireDERControlExchange() disarms the timer and tags the exchange name; no further sends occur on later ticks.

Summary: When the server declares EventStatus.currentStatus = Cancelled (2) on a poll, the client must cease the control immediately, report cancellation once if requested, and retire it.
Preconditions: An active/scheduled DERControl exists locally; a subsequent poll of the same control returns currentStatus = 2.
Actions:
1. Poll the DERControlList again with the control's currentStatus set to Cancelled.
2. Observe the DERControlResponse POST generated.
3. Inspect exchange state/timer after the transition.
Expected Results: DERCtrlState becomes CANCELLED immediately (no delay); a single "cancelled" DERControlResponse is sent if requested; control is retired (timer disarmed, name tagged) and does not re-fire.

Summary: When the server declares currentStatus = Cancelled With Randomization (3), the client must compute a single randomized cancellation instant using max(|randomizeStart|, |randomizeDuration|) as an END-only offset, keep running until that instant, then cancel and retire.
Preconditions: An active/scheduled DERControl with non-zero randomizeStart/randomizeDuration exists; poll returns currentStatus = 3.
Actions:
1. Poll with currentStatus = 3 and known randomizeStart/randomizeDuration values.
2. Observe DERCtrlState immediately after (should be CANCEL_PENDING, not CANCELLED).
3. Continue polling/ticking until CancelTime is reached.
4. Re-poll the same control again before CancelTime to confirm CancelTime is not redrawn.
Expected Results: CancelTime is computed once as anchor + max(|randomizeStart|,|randomizeDuration|) jitter, anchored on the server's EventStatus/dateTime where available; control remains CANCEL_PENDING (still active) until now >= CancelTime, then transitions to CANCELLED, sends the cancellation response once (if requested), and is retired. Re-polling does not redraw CancelTime.

Summary: When the server declares EventStatus.currentStatus = Superseded, the client must mark the control SUPERSEDED, report once if requested, and retire it from the active schedule.
Preconditions: An active/scheduled DERControl exists locally; a subsequent poll returns currentStatus = Superseded.
Actions:
1. Poll the DERControlList again with the control's currentStatus set to Superseded.
2. Observe the DERControlResponse POST generated.
3. Inspect exchange state/timer after the transition.
Expected Results: DERCtrlState becomes SUPERSEDED; a single "superseded" DERControlResponse is sent if requested; control is retired (timer disarmed, name tagged) and does not re-fire.

Summary: When a newer/higher-primacy DERControl overlaps an existing active control's window, ApplyDERControlSupersession() must mark the losing control SUPERSEDED and truncate its effective end, retiring it while leaving the winner active.
Preconditions: Two DERControls exist with overlapping schedule windows and different primacy/creationTime, both discovered from the same DERControlList.
Actions:
1. Discover a lower-precedence control first, let it become active.
2. Discover a higher-precedence/newer control overlapping its window.
3. Observe the supersession pass on the next tick.
4. Inspect both controls' states and EffectiveExpiry.
Expected Results: The losing control's EffectiveExpiry is truncated to the winner's start; it transitions to SUPERSEDED, sends a superseded response once (if requested), and is retired. The winning control remains active/unaffected and continues its own schedule.

Summary: When a full (non-paginated) DERControlList poll no longer includes an href previously spawned from that same list, the client must treat it as withdrawn: mark it cancelled, report cancellation, and retire it.
Preconditions: A DERControl was previously spawned from a DERControlList and is still active/scheduled locally; a subsequent poll of the SAME list (all == results) omits that control's href.
Actions:
1. Spawn/activate a DERControl from a DERControlList.
2. Re-poll the list with a response where "all" == "results" and the control's href absent.
3. Observe PruneStaleDERControls() behavior and the following tick.
Expected Results: The control is marked DERCTRL_STATE_CANCELLED, an INFO message is logged ("no longer published by the server; treating as cancelled..."), its timer is armed to fire immediately, and on the next tick EvaluateDERControlSchedule() sends the cancellation response (if requested) and retires it.

Summary: When a DERControlList poll response is paginated (all != results), the client must NOT treat any locally-active control as withdrawn, even if its href is absent from that page.
Preconditions: Multiple DERControls are active locally, spawned from one DERControlList; a poll returns a partial page where "all" != "results" and omits some of those hrefs.
Actions:
1. Configure/simulate a paginated DERControlList response ("all" != "results").
2. Re-poll with some previously-active hrefs missing from the page.
3. Observe whether PruneStaleDERControls() is invoked and its effect.
4. Inspect the Messages tab for a WARN diagnostic.
Expected Results: IsCompleteListResponse() returns FALSE; PruneStaleDERControls() is NOT called. No control is pruned or falsely cancelled. A WARN message is logged noting withdrawn-control detection was skipped for this poll.

Summary: Stale-control pruning must be scoped to the specific DERControlList polled (via OwnerListKey), never applied across all DERControlLists sharing the same client ID.
Preconditions: An EndDevice has two DERPrograms, each with its own DERControlList and its own active DERControl, both sharing the same client ID.
Actions:
1. Discover and activate one control from DERControlList A and another from DERControlList B (same client).
2. Poll DERControlList A only, with a complete response that omits A's control href but naturally does not include B's href either.
3. Observe which control(s) get pruned.
Expected Results: Only the control owned by the polled DERControlList (matching OwnerListKey) is evaluated/pruned; the control belonging to the other DERControlList is left untouched, even though its href was also absent from this particular list's response.

Summary: Once a terminal-state DERControlResponse (completed/cancelled/superseded) has been sent for a control, repeated ticks in the same terminal state must not resend it.
Preconditions: A DERControl has already reached a terminal state and its corresponding DERCtrlRespSent flag bit is set.
Actions:
1. Drive a control to a terminal state and confirm the response is sent once.
2. Force additional scheduler ticks / re-polls while the control remains in that terminal state.
3. Observe whether any further DERControlResponse POSTs occur.
Expected Results: No duplicate terminal DERControlResponse is sent on subsequent ticks; the control remains retired and RetireDERControlExchange() is idempotent (no repeated name-tag suffixing).

Summary: When a control reaches a terminal state but responseRequired does not request a specific response, the client must still retire the control from the active schedule, but must not POST a DERControlResponse.
Preconditions: A DERControl's responseRequired value excludes the specific-response bit (e.g., "00" or "01" only); the control reaches a terminal state (complete/cancelled/superseded).
Actions:
1. Configure a control with responseRequired not requesting specific response.
2. Drive it to a terminal state.
3. Observe whether a DERControlResponse POST occurs.
4. Inspect exchange state/timer afterward.
Expected Results: No DERControlResponse POST is sent for the terminal transition; an INFO suppress-reason message is logged; the control is still retired (timer disarmed, name tagged) via RetireDERControlExchange().

Summary: A DERControl whose operation mode the test set does not implement must be retired locally immediately on discovery, without being reported to the server as cancelled or superseded.
Preconditions: A DERControlList response contains a control whose opMode is not supported by this test set (ValidateAndReportDERCtrlOpMode returns FALSE).
Actions:
1. Configure/simulate a DERControl entry with an unsupported opMode.
2. Let SpawnOneDERChild() discover and spawn it.
3. Inspect the resulting exchange's state and name tag.
4. Confirm no DERControlResponse of cancelled/superseded type was sent.
Expected Results: The control is retired immediately via RetireDERControlExchange(child, "unsupported opMode"); no DERControlResponse reporting cancelled or superseded is sent, since the server's event itself is valid.

Summary: Cleanup logic (PruneStaleDERControls, EvaluateDERControlSchedule terminal handling) must remain correct and free of races/deadlocks when running concurrently with the response-parsing/polling thread under sustained load.
Preconditions: Multiple DERControls are active with a mix of states; the server is polled at high frequency (Read DER Control List) while scheduler ticks fire concurrently.
Actions:
1. Configure several active/terminal-bound DERControls.
2. Run sustained high-frequency polling alongside normal scheduler ticking for an extended interval.
3. Monitor for crashes, deadlocks, or corrupted exchange list state.
4. Inspect final state/response history for duplicates or inconsistencies.
Expected Results: No crashes, deadlocks, or data races occur (m_ExchPtrLock correctly guards shared state; message posting occurs outside the lock). No duplicate DERControlResponses are sent. The final active-control list is consistent with the latest server state.

Summary: Cleanup of stale/completed/superseded/cancelled DERControls must not disturb other still-active DERControls or unrelated function sets (regression check).
Preconditions: A mix of terminal, stale, and genuinely active DERControls exist concurrently; other IEEE 2030.5 function sets (e.g., DERSettings, Time, DefaultDERControl) are also in use.
Actions:
1. Run several poll cycles that cause some controls to complete/cancel/supersede/be pruned while others remain valid and active.
2. Exercise unrelated function set exchanges in parallel.
3. Inspect all active controls and other function sets' behavior afterward.
Expected Results: Only the targeted terminal/stale controls are cleaned up and retired; all other active controls continue executing on their original schedule uninterrupted, and unrelated function sets behave exactly as before this feature was introduced.

Summary: Cancelling an Active or Scheduled DERControl must stop it immediately, so it is no longer executed or acknowledged further.
Preconditions: A DERControl is currently Scheduled or Active in the schedule.
Actions:
1. Discover and schedule/activate a DERControl.
2. Update the server response so the control's EventStatus/currentStatus becomes Cancelled (value 2).
3. Re-poll the DERControlList/observe the next scheduling tick.
4. Continue polling afterward and observe behavior.
Expected Results:
1. On detecting the Cancelled status, the control transitions to Cancelled state immediately.
2. No further "started"/"completed" DERControlResponse POSTs are generated for the control on subsequent ticks.

Summary: When a Scheduled/Active DERControl is cancelled, exactly one DERControlResponse reporting currentStatus = "Cancelled" must be sent, provided the server requested a specific response.
Preconditions: A DERControl is Scheduled or Active with responseRequired requesting specific responses.
Actions:
1. Cancel a Scheduled/Active DERControl on the server (EventStatus/currentStatus = 2).
2. Observe the DERControlResponse POST generated on the next tick.
3. Continue polling and observe subsequent ticks.
Expected Results:
1. Exactly one DERControlResponse with currentStatus = "Cancelled" is sent once the cancellation is detected.
2. No further responses are sent for that control on later polls.

Summary: A DERControl that is cancelled (with or without randomization) before its StartTime has elapsed must still be correctly cancelled without ever incorrectly transitioning to Active.
Preconditions: A DERControl is Scheduled with a future StartTime and is cancelled before that StartTime arrives.
Actions:
1. Discover a DERControl with a StartTime a few minutes in the future.
2. Cancel it (plain or with randomization) before StartTime elapses.
3. Allow the original StartTime to pass and observe status.
Expected Results:
1. The control does not transition to Active at its original StartTime once cancellation is pending/applied.
2. The control's terminal state (Cancelled) is reached per the cancellation rule (immediate, or after the randomized boundary) regardless of the original StartTime.

Summary: Once a DERControl has reached the Cancelled terminal state and its cancellation acknowledgement has been sent, no further DERControlResponse POSTs should be generated for it, even on continued polling.
Preconditions: A DERControl has already been reported as Cancelled via a DERControlResponse.
Actions:
1. Allow a control to be cancelled and its "Cancelled" DERControlResponse sent.
2. Continue polling/ticking multiple times afterward.
3. Observe whether any further DERControlResponse POSTs occur for this control.
Expected Results: 1. No additional DERControlResponse (received/started/completed/cancelled) is sent for that control after its cancellation has been reported once.

Summary: If a DERControl is cancelled but the server's responseRequired does not request a specific response, the client must still transition the control to Cancelled internally while suppressing the DERControlResponse POST.
Preconditions: A DERControl with responseRequired not requesting specific responses is Scheduled/Active and is cancelled by the server.
Actions:
1. Configure a DERControl whose responseRequired does not request specific responses.
2. Cancel the control on the server.
3. Observe internal status and whether a DERControlResponse POST is sent.
Expected Results:
1. The control's internal state still transitions to Cancelled and is reflected in the tool/UI.
2. No DERControlResponse POST is sent for the cancellation, consistent with responseRequired.

Summary: A control that has already been Cancelled or is Cancel-Pending must remain exempt from being reopened even if the server subsequently republishes the same control with a different StartTime/ExpiryTime.
Preconditions: A DERControl is Cancelled (or Cancel-Pending with randomization) and the server later reports a changed StartTime/ExpiryTime for the same control on a later poll.
Actions:
1. Cancel a DERControl (plain or with randomization).
2. Re-poll the DERControlList with the server reporting an updated StartTime/ExpiryTime for the same control.
3. Observe whether the control's state is reopened to Scheduled.
Expected Results:
1. The cancelled (or cancel-pending) control's state is not reset to Scheduled by the rescheduled window.
2. The pending/committed cancellation still runs to completion as originally determined.

Summary: Read Time exchange completes successfully even without href tag.
Actions:
1. Perform the Read Time exchange with a server response that doesn’t have href tag
2. Observe the behaviour
Expected Results: Href is optional for Read time exchange and there is no crash

Summary: No validation error for Read Time exchange response without href tag.
Actions:
1. Perform the Read Time exchange with a server response that doesn’t have href tag
2. Observe the behaviour
Expected Results: No validation error for Read time exchange response without href tag

Summary: When two DERControls overlap in time, the one with the later creationTime must take precedence and execute, regardless of the primacy of the DERPrograms they belong to.
Preconditions: Two DERControls with overlapping time windows exist for the same client/EndDevice, issued by DERPrograms with different primacy values, where the later-issued (later creationTime) control belongs to the lower-primacy program.
Actions:
1. Configure two overlapping DERControls for the same EndDevice in different DERPrograms with different primacy values.
2. Give the lower-primacy program's control a later creationTime than the higher-primacy program's control.
3. Allow both controls' windows to become active and observe which control executes/reports Active.
Expected Results:
1. The control with the later creationTime is the one that remains Scheduled/Active and executes.
2. The earlier-issued (earlier creationTime) overlapping control does not execute during the overlapping window and is marked Superseded.

Summary: A DERControl fully covered from its own start by a later-issued overlapping control must be marked Superseded and must not execute or generate started/completed DERControlResponses.
Preconditions: A DERControl is Scheduled and a new overlapping DERControl with a later creationTime and a StartTime at or before the first control's StartTime is issued for the same EndDevice.
Actions:
1. Schedule a DERControl.
2. Issue a new, later-created overlapping DERControl whose StartTime covers the first control's window from its own start.
3. Observe the status of the earlier control and any DERControlResponse activity for it.
Expected Results:
1. The earlier control's status is updated to Superseded.
2. No "started"/"completed" DERControlResponse is generated for the superseded control; a "superseded" response is sent instead if requested.

Summary: Precedence handling for overlapping controls must not affect DERControls whose time windows do not overlap; each should be scheduled and executed independently in its own right.
Preconditions: Two DERControls exist for the same EndDevice with non-overlapping, sequential time windows, issued from programs with different primacy/creationTime.
Actions:
1. Configure two DERControls with sequential, non-overlapping StartTime/Duration windows for the same EndDevice.
2. Allow both to run to completion in sequence.
3. Observe status transitions and DERControlResponse activity for each.
Expected Results:
1. Both controls are scheduled, activated, and completed independently, each following its own normal lifecycle.
2. Neither control is marked Superseded, since their windows do not overlap.

Summary: A DERControl issued by a higher-primacy DERProgram must NOT automatically take precedence over an overlapping control from a lower-primacy program if the higher-primacy control's creationTime is earlier; precedence is based on recency of issue, not primacy.
Preconditions: Two DERControls overlap in time for the same EndDevice: Control A from a higher-primacy DERProgram issued earlier, Control B from a lower-primacy DERProgram issued later.
Actions:
1. Configure overlapping Control A (higher primacy, earlier creationTime) and Control B (lower primacy, later creationTime) for the same EndDevice.
2. Allow both windows to become active and observe which control executes.
Expected Results:
1. Control B (the later-issued control) executes and takes precedence despite belonging to the lower-primacy program.
2. Control A is marked Superseded (or truncated) even though its program has higher primacy.

Summary: A DERControl scheduled with a future StartTime must automatically transition to Active exactly when its StartTime is reached, independent of the configured poll rate for the DERControlList.
Preconditions: A DERControlList has been read and contains a control with a StartTime in the future. Time resource has already been read successfully from this server.
Actions:
1. Configure a DERControlList poll rate that is coarser than the time granularity needed.
2. Discover a DERControl whose StartTime is a few seconds/minutes away.
3. Wait for StartTime to elapse without triggering an additional manual poll of the list.
4. Observe the control's status and any DERControlResponse generated.
Expected Results:
1. The DERControl's internal status transitions from Scheduled to Active exactly at StartTime, driven by the scheduling engine's own timer rather than the list poll rate.
2. The transition occurs even if the next DERControlList poll has not yet occurred.

Summary: An Active DERControl must automatically transition to Complete when its duration elapses (EffectiveExpiry/ExpiryTime reached), independent of the DERControlList poll rate.
Preconditions: A DERControl is Active and its Duration/EffectiveExpiry is about to elapse. The DERControlList poll interval is longer than the remaining duration.
Actions:
1. Allow an Active DERControl to run until its Duration elapses, without forcing an intermediate list poll.
2. Observe the control's status immediately after the duration elapses.
3. Continue monitoring subsequent polls.
Expected Results:
1. The DERControl transitions from Active to Complete exactly when its duration ends, driven by the scheduling engine's timer.
2. The status update does not depend on, or wait for, the next DERControlList poll.

Summary: The tool must track and update DERControl status (Scheduled, Active, Complete) through its full lifecycle so the current state is always visible and correctly reflects the schedule.
Preconditions: A DERControl has been discovered and added to the schedule.
Actions:
1. Discover a DERControl with a future StartTime and observe its initial status.
2. Allow StartTime to elapse and observe the status update.
3. Allow the Duration to elapse and observe the final status update.
Expected Results:
1. Status is Scheduled before StartTime.
2. Status changes to Active once StartTime is reached.
3. Status changes to Complete once the duration/EffectiveExpiry is reached.
4. Each transition is reflected without manual intervention.

Summary: When a DERControl is first discovered/spawned, the client must send a "received" DERControlResponse immediately, before waiting for the event's StartTime to arrive.
Preconditions: Server has an active DERControlList with a control whose StartTime is in the future. Time resource has already been read successfully from this server.
Actions:
1. Configure/run a DERProgram exchange that discovers a DERControl scheduled to start later.
2. Allow the tool to dynamically spawn the Execute DER Control exchange.
3. Observe the first POST DERControlResponse sent by the tool.
4. Wait until the control's StartTime arrives and observe the next POST.
Expected Results:
1. The first DERControlResponse POST reports currentStatus = "Event received" immediately on discovery, prior to StartTime.
2. A second, separate DERControlResponse reporting "Event started" is sent only once StartTime is reached.

Summary: Once the "received" acknowledgement has been sent for a DERControl, re-polling the DERControlList for the same, unchanged control must not cause a second "received" DERControlResponse to be sent.
Preconditions: A DERControl has already had its "received" DERControlResponse sent and dispatched.
Actions:
1. Allow the "received" response to be sent for a discovered control.
2. Re-poll the DERControlList so the same control entry is parsed again, unchanged.
3. Observe whether another "received" DERControlResponse is generated.
Expected Results:
1. No duplicate "received" DERControlResponse is sent for the same control on subsequent, unchanged polls.
2. The control's schedule/state continues to progress normally afterward.

Summary: If the server's responseRequired attribute does not request a specific response for a transition, the client must not send a DERControlResponse for that transition, while still updating internal status.
Preconditions: A DERControl is discovered with responseRequired not requesting specific responses (e.g., 0x00 or receipt-only).
Actions:
1. Configure a DERControl whose responseRequired does not request a specific response for started/completed transitions.
2. Allow the control to activate and later complete.
3. Observe whether DERControlResponse POSTs are sent for these transitions.
Expected Results:
1. No "started"/"completed" DERControlResponse POST is sent when not requested.
2. The control's internal status (Active/Complete) still updates correctly and is reflected in the tool/UI.

Summary: Per IEEE 2030.5 9.2.3, the client must not act on (execute/acknowledge) a DERControl until a Time resource has been successfully retrieved from the same server.
Preconditions: A DERControlList response with a schedulable control is available, but the Read Time exchange for this server has not yet been run/completed.
Actions:
1. Discover a DERControl without first running the Read Time exchange for that server.
2. Observe whether any DERControlResponse POST is attempted.
3. Then run the Read Time exchange for the server and observe behavior afterward.
Expected Results:
1. No DERControlResponse is sent while no valid Time resource exists for the server; an informational message is logged/suppressed rather than a transmit error.
2. Once Time is retrieved, scheduling resumes and the appropriate response (received/started) is sent on the next tick.

Summary: The Read DER Control List exchange must read its own pollRate value from its response body rather than falling back to the pollRate configured on its parent Read DER Program List exchange.
Preconditions: Server responds to Read DER Control List with a pollRate value that differs from the parent Read DER Program List's pollRate.
Actions:
1. Configure the server/simulated response so DERControlList's pollRate differs from DERProgramList's pollRate.
2. Run the Read DER Program List exchange followed by Read DER Control List.
3. Inspect the poll interval used for subsequent Read DER Control List requests.
Expected Results: 1. Read DER Control List polls at the interval specified by its own response's pollRate attribute, not the pollRate inherited from the parent Read DER Program List exchange.

Summary: All acknowledgement transitions (received, started, completed/cancelled/superseded) for a given DERControl must be sent using the same dynamically-created Execute DER Control exchange rather than spawning a new exchange per transition.
Preconditions: A DERControl is discovered and dynamically spawns an Execute DER Control child exchange.
Actions:
1. Trigger the received, started, and completed transitions for the same DERControl in sequence (allow the full window to elapse).
2. Inspect the Exchange list / Messages tab for the exchange name associated with each POST.
Expected Results: 1. All three DERControlResponse POSTs (received, started, completed) are sent from the same single "Execute DER Control" exchange instance for that control; no additional duplicate exchanges are created for later transitions.

Summary: If the server changes a DERControl's StartTime/ExpiryTime on a later poll (a genuine reschedule), the client must re-open the state machine and re-evaluate transitions against the new window rather than keeping stale state from the old window.
Preconditions: A DERControl has already progressed (e.g., reported completed) against its original window, and the server subsequently republishes the same control with an extended/changed StartTime or ExpiryTime.
Actions:
1. Allow a control to complete against its original window.
2. Re-poll the DERControlList with the server now reporting a different StartTime/ExpiryTime for the same control.
3. Observe the control's status and any new DERControlResponse activity.
Expected Results:
1. The schedule fields (StartTime/ExpiryTime) are updated to the new values and an informational message notes the change.
2. The control's state resets to Scheduled (unless cancelled) and transitions are re-evaluated/re-reported against the new window.

Summary: Dynamic child exchange creation for DER Program List to DER Control List.
Preconditions:
Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, connected to an IEEE 2030.5 server exposing at least 2 DERProgram resources under a DERProgramList.
Under the DERProgram has DER Controls configured as well.
Actions:
1. File -> Select Protocol -> IEEE 2030.5
2. Configure/Enable "Read DER Program List" exchange and send the exchange.
3. Allow exchange to poll/respond
4. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: For each DERProgram href returned in the DERProgramList response, an appropriate "Read DER Control List" exchange is dynamically created and appended to the Exchange List. Name format: <TemplateBaseName>_Client <ClientID>_<EndDeviceID>

Summary: Dynamic child exchange creation for DER Program to DER Control List.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a discovered DER Program exchange whose response contains a DERControlList link.
Actions:
1. Allow "Read DER Program" exchange to receive a response.
2. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: One "Read DER Control List" child exchange are dynamically created from the same parent DER Program response

Summary: Dynamic child exchange creation for DER Control List to DER Control.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a discovered DER Control List exchange whose response contains one or more DERControl hrefs
Actions:
1. Allow "Read DER Control List" (dynamically created) exchange to receive a response.
2. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: One "Execute DER Control" child exchange is dynamically created per DERControl href found in the list

Summary: Dynamically-created exchange object list matches its static template.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a statically-configured "Read DER Program"/"Read DER Control"/"Read Default DER Control Settings" template exchange present in Protocol.xml
Actions:
1. Trigger discovery so a dynamic child of each type is spawned.
2. Double-click OR Right-click -> Exchange Properties on the dynamically-created exchange
Expected Results: The Application Layer Object Data structure (0:GET, response object) of the dynamically-created exchange is identical in layout to its corresponding static template exchange, only the request URL (href) and populated response values differ

Summary: Parsed response data is copied into dynamically-created child exchanges.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a DER Program List response already parsed for a specific DERProgram entry
Actions:
1. Allow dynamic "Read DER Program" child exchange to be created for that entry
2. Exchange Properties -> Object Properties on the response object
Expected Results: Field values already known from the parent's parsed sub-tree (mRID, description, links, href attributes) are pre-populated in the new child exchange's response object rather than left as placeholder "*" values

Summary: No duplicate exchanges are created for the same discovered href.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, with a dynamic child exchange already created for a given href
Actions: 1. Re-poll or re-parse the same parent response containing the same href
Expected Results: No additional exchange is created for that href; exchange count for the AP function remains unchanged

Summary: Client ID / End Device ID scoping on dynamically-created exchange names.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, connected to multiple Clients and/or End Devices, each exposing DER resources
Actions:
1. Trigger discovery across multiple clients/end devices.
2. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: Each dynamically-created exchange name follows the format <BaseName> <Index>_Client <ClientID>[_EndDevice <EndDevID>], correctly scoped to the client/end device that produced it (not shared across clients/devices)

Summary: Parent-child exchange hierarchy for End Device discovery chain.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, connected to a server exposing an EndDeviceList
Actions:
1. Enable "Read End Device List" exchange.
2. Allow discovery to proceed through End Device -> FSA List/DER List -> DER Program List chain.
3. View -> Exchange List
Expected Results: Exchanges are dynamically created in sequence: Read FunctionSet Assignments List and Read DER List (per End Device) and Read DER Program List (per FSA), and Read DER Control List (per Program List), and finally Read DER Control reflecting the discovered resource hierarchy

Summary: The dynamic exchanges are all created in a hierarchical manner when using the Config generator imported Index file and transmit enabled play functionality.
Preconditions: Have an instance of ASE2000 open in Exchange Mode, connected to a server.
Actions:
1. Import the Index file for configured end devices created from config generator.
2. Import the Comm file for config generator.
3. Hit the play button.
Expected Results: Exchanges are dynamically created in sequence: Read FunctionSet Assignments List and Read DER List (per End Device) and Read DER Program List (per FSA), and Read DER Control List (per Program List), and finally Read DER Control reflecting the discovered resource hierarchy after importing index file generated using config generator.

Summary: GET request is built correctly for a statically configured "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange with a bound href.
Preconditions: ASE2000 configured as IEEE 2030.5 client in Exchange Mode; "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange present with DLControl = GET and Object[0] href set to a valid DER Control resource URL (not */blank)
Actions:
1. File > Select Protocol > IEEE 2030.5
2. Configure "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange and trigger a Play/Send on the exchange.
3. Capture outgoing HTTP request
Expected Results: Request line is GET <href> HTTP/1.1 with no body; Content-Length/body absent; correct Host/port used from channel config.

Summary: GET request built for "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange communicates with the server and response received.
Preconditions: ASE2000 configured as IEEE 2030.5 client in Exchange Mode; "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange present with DLControl = GET and Object[0] href set to a valid DER Control resource URL (not */blank); simulator configured to return a well-formed XML body
Actions:
1. File > Select Protocol > IEEE 2030.5
2. Configure "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange and trigger a Play/Send on the exchange.
3. Capture incoming HTTP response
Expected Results: Proper response with necessery details is received and displayed in the line monitor.

Summary: The XML response received for "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange is correctly parsed and those supported are displayed in the object properties.
Preconditions: ASE2000 configured as IEEE 2030.5 client in Exchange Mode; "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange present with DLControl = GET and Object[0] href set to a valid DER Control resource URL (not */blank); simulator configured to return a well-formed XML body
Actions:
1. File > Select Protocol > IEEE 2030.5
2. Configure "Read FunctionSet Assignment" exchange and trigger a Play/Send on the exchange.
3. Inspect exchange Object properties values after response.
Expected Results: All expected fields are populated in the exchange's object data and visible in Property Grid; values match response XML exactly.

Summary: PollRate/pollRate attribute from response updates the exchange's transmission frequency.
Preconditions: Response contains a pollRate attribute (or exchange Object data has pollRate-tagged attribute)
Actions:

2. Observe exchange's configured frequency after processing.
Expected Results: IEEE2030_5Ex->PollRate updated to X

Summary: Supported operation mode opModConnect is accepted and executed when Execute DER Control exchange is sent manually.
Preconditions: Have a scheduled DERControl exchange whose DERControlBase specifies opModConnect
Actions:
1. Send the Execute DER Control of a particular end device.
2. View Messages/Line Monitor.
Expected Results: Execution proceeds and an acknowledgement POST request is supplied to the appropriate replyTo URI.

Summary: Supported operation modes like opModConnect is accepted and executed when Execute DER Control exchange is sent via transmit.
Preconditions: Have a scheduled DERControl exchange whose DERControlBase specifies a supported opMod function
Actions:
1. Send the Execute DER Control of a particular end device.
